abstract: Cognitive flexibility is the critical ability to adapt behavior in changing environments. Although traditionally associated with the prefrontal cortex, behavioral, lesion, and functional imaging evidence suggests the cerebellum contributes to cognitive flexibility. To test the role of the cerebellum at the circuit level, we paired widefield calcium imaging of single-cell Purkinje cells with a cognitive flexibility task and computational behavioral model. We find mid-posterior Purkinje cells encode all reinforcement learning parameters needed to produce flexible behavior, including specific representations for contingency degradation (CD) and enhancement (CE). Comparing somatic and dendritic encoding reveals a significant bias towards integrative multi-trial CD and CE representations in somas over long timescales, while dendrites encode more single-trial reward prediction errors. Activating lobule VIa, the region with strongest CD flexibility encoding, with patterned photostimulation causally expedites CD behavior. These results establish that the cerebellum extends beyond its canonical motoric functions to act as an important coordinator of cognitive flexibility behavior.
